purpose: Which control on each evaluated page plays which authentication role, for measuring the control-role classifier (authflowguard.evaluation.role_accuracy).
method: Established without running AuthFlowGuard. A, B and C were read from the fixture source in backend/authflowguard/evaluation_targets/; the markup is identical in secure and vulnerable modes, which change only server behaviour. Juice Shop (J) was taken from its known v20 markup and has not been checked against a running instance: every J entry is marked verified=false, to be confirmed on the first live run.
matching: A control is identified by stable attributes, never by its observed control-N number. Every key of a matcher must equal the observed control's value (text is compared ignoring case and repeated spaces); href_endswith must end the resolved link address. A role may list several matchers, any of which identifies the same control. Exactly one observed control must match, or the page's truth is reported as unresolved instead of being scored. A requested role mapped to null has no control on that page: any control the classifier gives that role is counted as extra.
steps: goto opens origin+path; fill types a named credential (never stored here as a role); click presses a control; click_if_present presses it only when it appears within two seconds; wait_for waits for a selector to be visible; wait_for_url waits for a URL glob. Steps use CSS selectors for setup only; they are not what is scored.

pages.derivation: login_form() renders the email input name=username and the password input name=password inside the form built by _form_page(), whose submit button is labelled with the page title 'Sign in'. _page() adds a nav with Login, Register (/register) and Reset password (/reset) links.
account() renders a POST /logout form with one button 'Log out'. The page has no menu toggle; the nav links are not account controls.

B.name: React/JSON bearer-token application with a one-time code

pages.derivation: _login_page() shows only the email input #username and the submit button #continue ('Continue'); there is no password field and no link. The code section is hidden until the email is accepted.

After #continue is pressed the #verification section is shown: the one-time-code input #verification-code and the button #verify ('Verify') that sends it. #continue stays visible but only restarts the first step.
_account_page() has no controls at all: no logout and no menu. Any answer here is extra.

entry() renders an untyped Member ID input name=member_id, a password input name=passphrase and the button 'Open my bookings'. The header's search box (name=q, type=search) is a distractor in another form. There is no registration or reset link.
bookings() renders a POST /desk/depart form with the button 'Log out of the desk'. There is no menu toggle; the header search box is not an account control.
